skill.name: ai-avatar-video
skill.description: Create AI avatar, talking head, lipsync, dubbing, and UGC-style videos with inference.sh belt CLI workflows.
skill.summary: Guides avatar video generation from portraits, scripts, audio, and dubbing workflows.
skill.author: 101-skills

security_audit.summary: The skill intentionally uses the belt CLI to run external avatar, TTS, transcription, and lipsync services. Most static hits are Markdown formatting or placeholder URLs, but the external command workflows, broad belt permission, and synthetic testimonial use case require user review.

remediation.suggestion: Limit allowed tools to the smallest set of belt commands needed for documented avatar workflows, if the host tool supports narrower allowlists.
Warn users before sending private images, audio, video, scripts, or signed URLs to inference.sh or related model providers.
Add guidance requiring consent, likeness rights, and clear disclosure for AI presenters, UGC ads, and testimonial-style videos.
Ask users to verify the source and version before running npx skills add commands for related skills or CLI setup.

semantic_findings.title: Broad External CLI Permission
semantic_findings.description: The skill declares allowed-tools as Bash(belt *), which permits any belt subcommand, not only the documented avatar workflows. A future or mistaken command could access broader belt functionality than users expect.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The frontmatter directly grants wildcard belt command access. The documented commands are legitimate, but the permission is broader than the specific workflows shown.

semantic_findings.title: Synthetic Testimonial And Presenter Abuse Risk
semantic_findings.description: The skill includes UGC-style avatar generation and sample testimonial language. Without consent and disclosure controls, this can support deceptive synthetic endorsements or impersonation-style marketing.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file explicitly targets UGC ads, virtual presenters, and generated testimonial-style scripts. The risk is contextual misuse rather than hidden code behavior.

content.value_statement: Producing talking-head video usually requires filming, voice work, and editing. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through avatar video workflows with inference.sh.
actual_capabilities: Creates avatar videos from portrait images and text scripts with P-Video-Avatar.
Uses audio files with OmniHuman, Fabric, PixVerse, or P-Video-Avatar workflows.
Generates portrait images before avatar creation with Pruna P-Image.
Builds dubbing workflows with transcription, translation, TTS, and lipsync steps.
Shows batch commands for multiple presenters and voice variants.
Links related inference.sh skills and documentation for deeper workflows.
limitations: Requires the belt CLI, an inference.sh account, and model access.
Sends prompts and media references to external services for processing.
Output quality depends on source image, audio clarity, and model choice.
Does not verify consent, likeness rights, or advertising disclosure rules.

use_cases.title: Product Demo Avatars
use_cases.description: Create short presenter videos for product launches, feature tours, and paid social campaigns.

use_cases.title: Training And Explainers
use_cases.description: Turn approved lesson scripts into consistent talking-head videos for courses and internal training.

use_cases.title: Localized Character Dialogue
use_cases.description: Generate speech, translate scripts, and lipsync characters for games or regional video versions.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner Avatar Intro
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a simple avatar from one portrait and one script.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the ai-avatar-video skill to create a short avatar introduction from my portrait and script. Recommend the simplest model and settings.

prompt_templates.title: Product Demo Presenter
prompt_templates.scenario: Build a branded talking-head video for a product workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the skill to plan a 30-second product demo avatar. Include voice style, resolution, model choice, and required media inputs.

prompt_templates.title: Dubbing Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Localize an existing video into another language.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the skill to create a dubbing workflow for my video. Include transcription, translated speech generation, and lipsync steps.

prompt_templates.title: Batch UGC Variants
prompt_templates.scenario: Create multiple avatar ad variants from one campaign brief.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the skill to design a batch UGC workflow with three presenters, distinct voices, and disclosure-safe testimonial wording.

output_examples.input: Create a 30-second onboarding avatar from a portrait and approved script.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends P-Video-Avatar, selects a matching voice, chooses 720p or 1080p, and lists the required image and script inputs.

output_examples.input: Dub a product video into Spanish with a new voice track.
output: Lipsync the original video with the new audio.

output_examples.input: Produce three UGC-style avatar variants for one campaign.
output_examples.output: The skill outlines a batch workflow with three approved presenters, voice prompts, video prompts, and disclosure-aware script variants.

best_practices: Use consented, high-quality, front-facing images with clear lighting.
Review every script for accuracy, consent, and synthetic media disclosure needs.
Start with P-Video-Avatar, then switch models only for specific lipsync or multi-character needs.
anti_patterns: Do not use a real person likeness without permission.
Do not upload confidential footage, private audio, or signed URLs to external services.
Do not present synthetic testimonials as verified customer statements.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It helps create AI avatar, talking-head, lipsync, dubbing, and UGC-style videos using belt CLI workflows.

faq.question: Which model should I try first?
faq.answer: Start with P-Video-Avatar for most portrait plus script workflows because it includes built-in text-to-speech.

faq.question: Can I use my own audio?
faq.answer: Yes. Several workflows accept an audio URL for lipsync or audio-driven avatar generation.

faq.question: Does it work without inference.sh?
faq.answer: No. The documented workflows require belt CLI access to inference.sh apps and related model providers.

faq.question: Can it make multilingual videos?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes workflows for transcription, translated speech generation, and lipsync in another language.

faq.question: What should I check before publishing?
faq.answer: Confirm consent, likeness rights, factual claims, and any required synthetic media disclosure.
